history.rationale: Ablates the N-glycan at position N236 (standard N306), unshielding the attachment surface and significantly enhancing F-triggering and viral entry efficiency. This mutant has been experimentally demonstrated to confer a hyperfusogenic phenotype.

Removes the N-glycan at position N411 (standard N481), which relieves steric constraints on the head domain and facilitates conformational activation of the F fusion machinery. Experimental studies confirm substantial increases in cell-cell fusion and entry.

Eliminates the N-glycan at position N308 (standard N378), enhancing receptor accessibility and entry kinetics without compromising overall glycoprotein expression or stability. This substitution yields marked hyperfusogenicity in cell-cell fusion assays.

Conservatively eliminates the N236 glycosylation site while preserving polar side-chain volume, preventing glycan-mediated steric hindrance of F-protein triggering. It reproduces the hyperfusogenic entry phenotype of the alanine substitution.

Maintains side-chain polarity while eliminating the bulky N411 glycan moiety, enhancing trigger competence for F-mediated fusion. This conservative substitution maintains structural stability while promoting cell entry.

Removes the N-glycan at position N459 (standard N529) adjacent to the ephrin-binding pocket, reducing steric barriers to receptor engagement and accelerating fusion triggering. This modification enhances entry efficiency on target cells.
A conservative substitution that abolishes glycosylation at N308 without altering regional backbone flexibility. This promotes receptor-induced conformational signaling to the F fusion machinery.
Eliminates the N459 glycan while preserving local hydrogen-bonding capacity near the ephrin-binding interface. This improves receptor engagement kinetics and entry activation.

Disrupts the N236-S237-T238 glycosylation sequon at the +2 position, preventing glycan addition at N236 while leaving the asparagine residue intact. This recapitulates the entry-enhancing effect of N236 de-glycosylation.
Abolishes the N411-N412-T413 sequon via threonine substitution, preventing core N-glycosylation at N411. This unshields the G head domain and promotes efficient F-triggering during viral entry.
